en.body:
## 1. The Love Hypothesis
Based on Ali Hazelwood's beloved novel, this rom-com dives into the quirky world of academia. It follows a Ph.D. candidate who impulsively kisses a notoriously intimidating professor, sparking an unexpected connection. The chemistry between Lili Reinhart and Tom Bateman promises a delightful, witty romance.

## 2. The Runner
Gal Gadot stars as an attorney racing against time to save her son in this high-octane thriller directed by Kevin Macdonald. While critical reception has been mixed, its gripping premise and Gadot's star power have made it a buzzy hit on the platform. Expect a fast-paced chase across London.

## 3. Backrooms
Delving into the unsettling world of internet creepypasta, this film explores a terrifying dimension of endless, liminal spaces. It taps into a viral phenomenon, offering a unique blend of psychological horror and survival. If you're looking for something genuinely unnerving, this is it.

## 4. The Great Escape
This classic wartime drama transports viewers to a World War II German POW camp. It chronicles the elaborate and daring escape plan hatched by Allied prisoners. Its enduring legacy lies in its thrilling narrative and testament to human resilience.

## 5. The Devil's Mouth (2026)
For fans of creature features and star-studded casts, this 2026 release offers a thrilling dive into terror. With appearances from Lana Condor and Kathryn Newton, the film promises suspense set within claustrophobic caves. It's a modern horror flick with plenty of bite.

## 6. Toy Story 5
While details are scarce, the mere mention of "Toy Story 5" is enough to excite fans worldwide. This installment promises to continue the beloved Pixar saga, bringing back Woody, Buzz, and the gang for new adventures. Expect the signature blend of humor and heart that has defined the franchise.

## 7. Untitled Thriller (2026)
This intriguing thriller, directed by Derek Cianfrance, sneaks up on you with its sophisticated blend of humor and dread. It masterfully navigates tonal shifts, starting with lighthearted moments before evolving into something far more squirm-inducing. Its emotional payoffs are well worth the ride.
Bottom Line: This week's Prime Video lineup offers a compelling mix of genres, ensuring there's a perfect watch for every mood.

content_raw: The number one movie on Prime Video this week is the new Gal Gadot action thriller The Runner . Directed by Kevin Macdonald and written by Mark Gibson , the movie follows attorney Maia Martin (Gadot) as she races across London to save her son. Despite getting largely negative reviews from critics, the film has been performing quite well on Prime Video since its release last week. However, if that’s not quite your cup of tea, there are still plenty of other options to explore on the platform. Without further ado, here’s a look at three great movies that we think you should watch on Prime Video this week.
